OWNER RULE 2026-10-06 (supersedes minimum-change iteration): close with margin in ONE step; do not iterate one class per round.
- On every class that has failed, or is within ~50 ps of failing, in setup at SS: add a pipeline register stage now (+1 cycle; +2 where the path crosses >= ~400 um or a macro channel). Pair each added stage with duplicated (kept) drivers on any net with >= ~64 loads, and place the register at the far end of the long wire / at the macro pin.
- Also stage every block-crossing bus and every macro output to the next register up front. Don't wait to see it fail.
- Pre-approved cost: <= ~2% on the headline (AR/MTP) per lever. Measure the cycle cost, record it in the lever record and recompose. If a version would exceed 2%, say so in STATUS and run it anyway alongside a leaner one.
- Keep the current leaner routes running only if they are already past CTS; launch the margin version in parallel on other hosts NOW (3-4 variants: density / aspect / buffer budget).
- Hold (FF) problems are not fixed by extra stages: keep handling them with the hold repair / useful-skew budget.
- Exact bench + negative controls are still mandatory for every changed RTL before adoption.

ADDENDUM (owner, 2026-10-06): block closure must SURVIVE die integration. Closing at +3 ps is not closed.
- Sign-off target for the three hard blocks (PQ spine, PQ q-element, HBM attention tile), and for every new block view: SS setup slack >= +60 ps at the block level (route with the SDC over-constrained to ~770 ps or less, sign off at 833.333 ps). FF hold >= +15 ps.
- Every block boundary is register-to-register: inputs captured in a flop at the input pin, outputs launched from a flop at the output pin, no logic between pin and flop. Then die-level paths are only pin-to-pin wire, which die stations can stage.
- IO constraints budget a die clock-arrival difference of >= 150 ps against the block's measured insertion, plus a wire allowance to the nearest die station.
- Add as many pipeline cycles as this needs. Cost <= ~2% per lever is pre-approved; above that, report and continue.
- After block closure, run die-context STA with the real abstract (the S81 re-run for DS, the HBM abstracts die for attention) before declaring adoption.

CLARIFICATION (Claude decision, 2026-10-06 ~10:40, applies to ALL blocks): the die clock-arrival IO term is 150 ps only on ports that cross a die wire to a DIFFERENT clock region. Ports between blocks in the SAME clock region use the measured region pair skew + margin (Qwen: 90 ps = 65 measured + 25). Hold is closed by hold repair under FF-corner constraints (FF insertion, 50 ps hold IO uncertainty), never with RTL registers. Never put a register inside a one-cycle loop to meet IO budgets: move the hierarchy cut so the loop stays inside one hardened block.

OWNER UPDATE (2026-10-06 18:15 PT): ACCEPTANCE LINE LOWERED. A block is CLOSED at SS >= +15 ps and FF >= +15 ps at the 833.333 ps sign-off (60/25 corners), with the agreed die-clock IO budgets (150 ps inter-region, measured + margin intra-region, FF hold model) and DRC 0. The design target stays generous (route at ~770 ps), but do NOT redesign or re-route a block that already meets +15/+15. Re-check every harvested result against this line now: anything that passes is closed, so collect, export and merge it.

OWNER (2026-10-06 18:20 PT): SMALLER BLOCKS. Cap hardened blocks at about 0.5-1 mm on a side, joined by registered pin-to-pin hops; split any block that fails structurally (deep clock tree, cross-block cones). SCRIPTED CLOSURE LOOP: once /tmp/claude-review-20261003/CLOSURE_LOOP_HOWTO exists, register routes there as job JSON instead of babysitting them with agents.

OWNER (2026-10-06 18:25 PT): QWEN ROM IS CLOSED. Do not start or continue any Qwen ROM work: die, elements, token, KV_MAP, pilots. All Claude Qwen jobs are stopped. Focus: the DeepSeek ROM array and the HBM accelerator only.

STANDARD FLOW (Claude decision, 2026-10-06 18:35): IO constraints MUST use each block's MEASURED clock insertion. Run CTS-only calibration -> measure SS/FF insertion -> regenerate the IO SDC (common/make_io_vclk_ff.sh + stn_io_min.py) -> route. A copied/assumed insertion caused 10^5 hold buffers and congestion on glue, head, BF and softmax. Recalibrating a constraint is a correctness fix, not a settings sweep.

DESIGN SIMPLIFICATION RULES (Claude decision, 2026-10-06 19:00 PT; apply to EVERY non-closing block in ONE pass):
1. EXACTNESS = TRANSACTION-LEVEL, not cycle-level. Results, ordering and fault detection must match the original exactly (numerics and token results stay mandatory), but latency MAY increase. Rewrite lockstep benches as scoreboard/transaction compares where needed, and keep the negative controls.
2. Every block interface is latency-insensitive: registered valid/ready with a 2-slot skid, or credits. No combinational pin-to-pin path; no same-cycle cross-block handshake.
3. Every reduction over more than 4 inputs (fault OR, all-banks AND, top-k, compare trees) gets one register level per 4-6 gate levels.
4. Fault/veto may land 1-2 cycles later IF nothing it protects can commit in between: hold the commit (publication/retire) until the registered fault result is known. The CP's 3-edge fault latency is the precedent.
5. Fanout > 32 gets kept replicas; every SRAM/ROM macro output gets a register at the macro; blocks <= ~1 mm; IO SDC at the measured insertion.
Price the added cycles in each block's record; report cost per block. Don't preserve legacy same-cycle behaviour at the cost of closure.

OWNER-APPROVED (2026-10-06 ~20:30 PT, CLAUDE BUDGETS): close each block against its budget sheet (results/rtl/budgets_20261006/sheets/<master>.json; tools/budgets/make_block_sdc.py; closure-loop job "budget": {"master": ...}). The calibrate stage is a CHECK against the sheet (NEEDS_BUDGET on deviation), not a re-calibration. See BUDGETS_README.md.

OWNER EXCEPTION (2026-10-06 ~20:50): the Qwen ROM DIE-TOP DETAILED ROUTE is restarted (one dedicated agent). Everything else about Qwen ROM stays closed: no element redesigns, no token work.

OWNER (2026-10-06 ~21:00): for die-level relay stations and wire hops, take the FASTEST path to closure: add stages/cycles die-wide with a conservative pitch (~300 um or less), rather than optimising the pitch. A performance loss of a few percent is accepted.

OWNER (2026-10-06 ~21:45): the Qwen ROM die-top work is RESUMED, concurrent with DS/HBM: insert relay stations on long die wires (closed Qwen station views, ~300 um pitch, cost accepted), fix the east-seam pin funnel, then GRT -> DRT -> die STA. Qwen element redesigns are still NOT allowed.

BUDGETS_README.md.text:
# BUDGETS README: top-down timing budgets and the planned die clock (all agents; 2026-10-06, CLAUDE BUDGETS)

**Rule (OWNER_RULE_MARGIN_FIRST):** close each block against its budget sheet.

Code: `tools/budgets/` (branch claude/budgets-20261006, merged to main). Record: `results/rtl/budgets_20261006/`
(README.md, SUMMARY.md, sheets/, clock_plan/).

## What exists
1. **Die clock plan** (`clock_plan/<die>.json.gz`), for HBM r16j and S81 r9m215_v4 (scan / layer1 / head).
   - Structure: PLL -> buffered M8/M9 H-tree trunk per domain -> clock-region roots (padded to the slowest region of
     the tree) -> region trees -> partition clock pins.
   - Regions: S81 field columns use the cfifo `co` trees. Other regions are at most 4 mm, merged along synchronous nets
     up to 5.25 mm.
   - Validated by a clock-only OpenROAD CTS run on EPYC3, with the partition clock pins as sinks (0.3-0.7 GB, seconds).
   - Measured:

     | die | trunk SS / FF (ns) | region bounds | worst unresolved crossing |
     |---|---|---|---|
     | HBM | 2.69 / 1.43 | <= 57 ps | 268 ps |
     | S81 | 3.86 / 2.05 | <= 50 ps; columns 351-388 ps insertion, <= 38 ps skew | 385 ps |

   - Intra-region budgets are set per region (measured + 25, capped at 90), and come out at 29-90 ps (columns 54-63).
   - Inter-region stays 150 ps. Forwarded-clock hops take 0 ps on setup.
   - The crossings still above 150 ps are listed in the record README: hub vm/index/router/cmdproc on HBM;
     selector/collector <-> hub end blocks and ctrl <-> svc on S81. They need a forwarded clock, a meso FIFO or a
     region re-cut.
2. **Budget sheets** (`sheets/<master>.json`): 257 masters.
   - Coverage: HBM 74, including all 71 masters of index.json; S81 165 die masters; S81-PH 18 tiles.
   - Each interface gives:
     - the length to the next register;
     - the skew class;
     - the SS input and output delay, with the fraction of 833.333 and the internal budget;
     - FF min delays;
     - stages needed against stages planned;
     - pin registration;
     - die fanout.
   - Each block gives:
     - the clock-pin arrival target (the die compensates the block's own insertion);
     - an internal insertion TARGET, min(430 + 0.865 sqrt(wh), 900) ps;
     - measured calibrations where they exist.
   - SUMMARY.md lists the 154 interfaces that are infeasible as planned: they need stations or architecture.
3. **SDC generator**: `python3 tools/budgets/make_block_sdc.py sdc|ff|check <master>`.
   - `sdc` writes the block IO SDC from the sheet. It replaces `make_io_vclk*.sh` at an assumed or copied insertion.
     `--route-mode route` uses 123 ps (the 770 route target); `signoff` uses 60 ps.
   - `ff` writes the FF hold post-SDC.
   - `check` compares the measured insertion with the sheet.
4. **Closure loop**: add `"budget": {"master": "<master>", "clock": "core_clk"}` to the job JSON.
   - The loop generates `$BUDGET_SDC` (route), `$BUDGET_SDC_SIGNOFF` and `$BUDGET_SDC_FF` from the sheet on main, and
     exports `$BUDGET_SHEET` and `$BUDGET_LINT_SS/FF`.
   - Point your `sdc_cmd` / route at them, e.g. `cp $BUDGET_SDC <view>/io.sdc`, instead of `make_io_vclk_margin.sh
     $CK_SS_MEAN`.
   - Calibrate stays a CHECK. If the measured SS insertion is off the sheet value, or over the block TARGET, by more
     than 100 ps, the job stops as NEEDS_BUDGET and is never silently re-calibrated.
   - Then either fix the block tree (smaller block, pin-near clock entry), or re-plan the block's die entry target in
     the sheet (rerun budget_sheet.py with the calibration) and run `closure_loop.py retry <job>`. The retry continues
     on the sheet SDC.
   - Option `"on_deviation": "continue"` only flags the deviation in the ledger and carries on.

## How to use it as a block owner
- Read your sheet before RTL or floorplan work:
  - `interfaces[].feasible == false`: add the stations or change the architecture first.
  - `stages_needed`: the pipeline count per interface.
  - `clock.internal_insertion.target_ss`: the CTS depth your block must meet.
- Every data pin is a flop at the pin. Control nets carry at most 32 loads; use kept replicas above that.
- Domain ports: if your block has a second real clock (for example a CDC block with `hbm_clk`), pass
  `--domain-clock <period>=<clock>`, or `"domain_clock": ["1023.96=hbm_clk"]` in the job.

## Regenerating
```
python3 tools/budgets/extract_die.py --src <git archive of the generator commit> --die s81r8_layer --s81-opts "..." --out M.json.gz
python3 tools/budgets/clock_plan.py emit --die-model M.json.gz --group htop|hreg|region --out CASE ; CASE/run.sh (EPYC3)
python3 tools/budgets/clock_plan.py record --die-model M.json.gz --case CASE... --out plan.json
python3 tools/budgets/collect_calib.py --extra results/rtl/budgets_20261006/inputs/calib_extra.json --out calibrations.json
python3 tools/budgets/budget_sheet.py --die NAME=M.json.gz:plan.json.gz ... --calib calibrations.json --tiles tiles.json --out results/rtl/budgets_20261006
```
Re-run the sheet after a floorplan round (a new generator commit) or after new calibrations.
